questions.text: Why does the text say the passive was "invented" for process descriptions?
opts: The process matters more than who performs each step
questions.correct: The process matters more than who performs each step
questions.hint: "Usually more interested in the process than in who is performing each step."

questions.text: What does "The cotton is picked" emphasise compared to "Workers pick the cotton"?
opts: The universal process, not the actor
questions.correct: The universal process, not the actor
questions.hint: "The passive removes the actor from view and focuses attention on the object and the action."

questions.text: The text says the passive voice is always bad or weak writing.
questions.hint: "There is a common myth that passive voice is always 'bad'..." — the text calls this a myth.

questions.text: "Mistakes were made" is an example of ___ use of the passive.
questions.hint: "Mistakes were made" is described as "evasive" — it avoids naming who made the mistakes.

questions.text: The text says passive appears in news, academic writing, and official notices.
opts: In news, academic writing, and official notices
questions.correct: In news, academic writing, and official notices
questions.hint: "They appear in news reports... academic writing... official notices..."

questions.text: What is the "invisible agent" mentioned in the text?
opts: The missing "by whom" in a passive sentence
questions.correct: The missing "by whom" in a passive sentence
questions.hint: "That invisible agent — the missing 'by...' — is often the most interesting thing of all."

questions.text: What is the first step in the WKU workshop process?
questions.hint: "All products are first designed on a computer."

questions.text: Who reviews the designs before printing?
questions.hint: "They're reviewed by supervisors."

questions.text: In the WKU workshop, products are assembled by robots.
questions.hint: "The product is assembled here, by students." / "assembled by hand, not by machine."

questions.text: What happens to finished products that pass inspection?
opts: Photographed and stored in a showcase; displayed at exhibition
questions.correct: Photographed and stored in a showcase; displayed at exhibition
questions.hint: "Photographed and stored in our showcase. The best ones are displayed at the end-of-year exhibition."

questions.text: The prototype is tested for stress, ___, and heat.
questions.hint: "Stress tests, weight tests, heat tests." — three tests mentioned.

questions.text: Has a student project ever been used commercially?
opts: Only once, adapted by a local company
questions.correct: Only once, adapted by a local company
questions.hint: "One was adapted and used by a local company last year."

questions.text: The passive voice is formed with:
questions.hint: Passive = TO BE (correct form) + PAST PARTICIPLE. Always!

questions.text: "The bridge was built in 1850." This is:
questions.hint: "WAS built" = was/were + past participle = past simple passive.

questions.text: "The products ___ every morning." (check — present passive)
questions.hint: Present passive: "The products ARE CHECKED every morning." ✅

questions.text: "The results will be announced tomorrow." — Future passive uses:
questions.hint: Future passive: WILL + BE + past participle. "Will BE ANNOUNCED." ✅

questions.text: "The letter was wrote by her." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: ✅ "The letter was WRITTEN by her." — "write" → past participle = "written", never "wrote"!

questions.text: "My car was stolen." — Why passive?
opts: Unknown agent — we don't know who stole it
questions.correct: Unknown agent — we don't know who stole it
questions.hint: Unknown agent → passive is natural. "My car was stolen." ✅

questions.text: "The problem ___ (solve — modal passive: can)."
questions.hint: Modal passive: modal + BE + past participle. "The problem CAN BE SOLVED." ✅

questions.text: Convert to passive: "Workers built the mosque."
questions.hint: Past active → past passive. "The mosque WAS BUILT." ✅

questions.text: "The parts are assembled." "Assembled" means:
questions.hint: "assemble" = to fit parts together to make a complete object.

questions.text: "All products are inspected before delivery." "Inspected" means:
opts: Looked at carefully to check quality
questions.correct: Looked at carefully to check quality
questions.hint: "inspect" = to examine carefully, especially to check quality or safety.

questions.text: The passive ___ technical and scientific writing.
questions.hint: "Passive constructions DOMINATE technical writing, science, and manufacturing descriptions."

questions.text: "The data is processed." "Processed" means:
questions.hint: "process" = to handle or deal with data/materials using a defined method.

questions.text: "The writer chose to emphasise the result." "Emphasise" means:
opts: Give special importance or attention to
questions.correct: Give special importance or attention to
questions.hint: "emphasise" = to give special importance to something; to highlight it.
